approachQuestion.prompt:
Peak Request Burst

Sorted integer array `times` gives request timestamps, including repeated timestamps for separate requests. For a fixed positive width, return the greatest number of requests that can lie in a half-open real-time interval [start,start+width). You may choose any real start. Return zero when no requests exist.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ times[i] ≤ 10^12; 1 ≤ width ≤ 10^12.
• times is sorted non-decreasingly and read-only. Every array entry counts separately, even for equal timestamps. Use 64-bit arithmetic.

Examples:
1. times = [1,1,4,5], width = 4 → 3, using [1,5).
2. times = [0,5], width = 5 → 1, because no width-five half-open interval contains both.
3. times = [], width = 1 → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: times is sorted non-decreasingly and read-only. Every array entry counts separately, even for equal timestamps. Use 64-bit arithmetic.

options.text: Move right through the sorted timestamps. Advance left while times[right]-times[left] is at least width. Record the greatest right-left+1 after repair.
options.feedback: A set of sorted timestamps fits in a width-sized half-open interval exactly when its last-first span is strictly smaller than width. Duplicate entries remain separate requests.

options.text: For each right endpoint binary-search the first earlier timestamp strictly greater than times[right]-width, then maximize the resulting count.
options.feedback: This strict inequality correctly handles the half-open boundary, but repeats searches for a left boundary that only advances.

options.text: Accept all segments with last-first span at most width.
options.feedback: For [0,5] and width=5 this counts both, although the interval includes its start and excludes its end.

options.text: Remove duplicate timestamps before computing the largest number of distinct timestamps in any interval.
options.feedback: For [2,2,2] and width=1 all three requests count; deduplication changes the answer to one.

feedback.reason: The half-open time interval excludes events exactly width units after its start.
details: Scan right in order. While times[right]-times[left] ≥ width, increment left. Then update best from right-left+1. Keep only the two boundaries and best count; do not create or deduplicate interval contents.

The half-open time interval excludes events exactly width units after its start. Therefore equality in span>=width requires removing the left event. Equal timestamps are separate events and must not be deduplicated.

“Move right through the sorted timestamps. Advance left while times[right]-times[left] is at least width. Record the greatest right-left+1 after repair.”: A set of sorted timestamps fits in a width-sized half-open interval exactly when its last-first span is strictly smaller than width. Duplicate entries remain separate requests.

“For each right endpoint binary-search the first earlier timestamp strictly greater than times[right]-width, then maximize the resulting count.”: This strict inequality correctly handles the half-open boundary, but repeats searches for a left boundary that only advances.
“Accept all segments with last-first span at most width.”: For [0,5] and width=5 this counts both, although the interval includes its start and excludes its end.
“Remove duplicate timestamps before computing the largest number of distinct timestamps in any interval.”: For [2,2,2] and width=1 all three requests count; deduplication changes the answer to one.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Maintain a strict timestamp span” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sorted-time boundaries advance once each while preserving the strict span rule.
details: Sorted timestamps make every feasible interval correspond to consecutive entries. It fits exactly when its span is less than width; starting at its earliest timestamp constructs a valid half-open interval. Each boundary advances at most n times, with constant scalar state.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Sorted timestamps permit each boundary to advance once; the method does not test a new full event scan for every interval start.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: No sorting or copied event array is part of this fixed method because input timestamps are already ordered.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Only left, right, and best count are retained; individual qualifying intervals are never stored.
